Notes from a measured turn
The welfare officer opened the meeting by raising comfort stops. Mina Clark and Jonah Ramos attended with the team from Aurelia Skyways, along with Milo's file under review. The group kept the focus on steady handling, clear handovers, and calm wording at the counter so pet travelers do not pick up stress from the desk process.

The senior coordinator reviewed routine intake checks and reminded everyone to confirm carrier fit, water access, and leash control before any move through the terminal. Staff were told to watch for signs of fatigue, heat, or fear and to slow the pace when an animal needs a break. If a traveler arrives uneasy, the first response should be simple reassurance, then a quiet space, then a stepwise review before any escalation.

Discussion also covered record notes for each case. The team agreed that short, plain entries help avoid confusion and make later checks easier. When a concern appears minor, staff should still log what was seen, what was offered, and how the traveler responded. If the issue grows, the matter should pass through the calm review path without delay or debate at the front desk.

The meeting closed with a reminder to keep the Companion Animal Travel Desk tidy, predictable, and patient in every exchange. The meeting ended.
